platforms.web: Website or web app in the browser
platforms.desktop: Desktop app for Windows, macOS or Linux
platforms.service: Backend service or API without its own UI

traits.backend: Has its own server logic or API
traits.database: Stores structured data in a database
traits.accounts: Users sign up and log in
traits.i18n: More than one language or locale
traits.location: Uses maps or the device location
traits.public: Launched to the public: marketing, store or search visibility
traits.eu_users: Has users in the EU (GDPR applies in addition to Swiss law)
traits.cross_platform: One shared codebase for several platforms

stations.title: Idea
stations.goal: The problem, the users, the success signal, the non-goals and the platforms are clear.

stations.title: Concept
stations.goal: The MVP is defined as prioritised user stories and testable done scenarios.

stations.title: Design
stations.goal: Every MVP screen has a flow, a layout, its states and design tokens with numbers.

stations.title: Architecture
stations.goal: Stack, layers, data, interfaces, secrets and environments are decided and sourced.

stations.title: Plan
stations.phase: D, E, F, G, H, I
stations.goal: A task DAG covers every build item, the first briefs are written and the cold start passes.

stations.title: Build
stations.goal: Every build item is delivered by a done task with recorded gate evidence and a passing review.

stations.title: Verify
stations.goal: The whole product passes its tests, device/browser matrix, accessibility and security checks.

stations.title: Release
stations.goal: The product ships from a clean tag with legal texts, store listings and a tested rollback.

stations.title: Operate
stations.goal: Errors, uptime, backups, costs, support and updates are watched and owned.

items.title: Problem and goal
items.detail: What the software solves and for whom, in 3–6 sentences.

items.title: Target users
items.detail: Who uses it, in which situation and on which device.

items.title: Success signal
items.detail: What visibly shows after four weeks that it works.

items.title: Non-goals
items.detail: What the project deliberately does not do, and what comes later.

items.title: Platform decision
items.detail: Web, iOS, Android, desktop, CLI or service, with the reason; recorded in factory.json.

items.title: Budget and time
items.detail: Build budget, deadline and the monthly running-cost ceiling.

items.title: Repository recon
items.detail: Facts about the existing repo: stack, commands, conventions, debt, what must not be touched.

items.title: Personas
items.detail: One to three user profiles with goal, context and frustration.

items.title: Prioritised feature list
items.detail: Every feature marked MVP, next or later; the MVP is the smallest useful product.

items.title: User stories
items.detail: 'As a … I want … so that …' for every MVP feature, with acceptance in WHEN–THEN.

items.title: Definition of done
items.detail: Three to five end-to-end scenarios D1..Dn that must work at launch.

items.title: Alternatives
items.detail: Two or three existing solutions and what this one does differently.

items.title: Running costs
items.detail: Hosting, services, store fees and API usage per month at the expected scale.

items.title: Data inventory
items.detail: Which data, its source, owner, retention period and how it is deleted.

items.title: Legal frame
items.detail: Applicable law (Swiss revFADP; GDPR with EU users), terms of the APIs used, licences.

items.title: Monetisation
items.detail: Free, one-off, subscription or in-app purchase; platform fees (stores take 15–30 %).

items.title: Top risks
items.detail: The three biggest risks and how the plan reduces each.

items.title: User flows
items.detail: How a user gets from start to goal for every MVP story, including the error path.

items.title: Wireframes
items.detail: Rough layout of every MVP screen (sketch, image or ASCII).

items.title: Mockups
items.detail: Final visual design of the key screens.

items.title: Prototype test
items.detail: A clickable prototype tried by one to three target users; findings recorded.

items.title: Design system
items.detail: Colours, type scale, spacing, radii, icons and components as named tokens with values.

items.title: Screen states
items.detail: Empty, loading, error, offline, success and disabled for every screen.

items.title: Light and dark mode
items.detail: Both colour schemes defined as tokens.

items.title: Accessibility
items.detail: Contrast ≥ 4.5:1, scalable text, screen-reader labels, focus order, touch targets ≥ 44 pt.

items.title: Onboarding
items.detail: First-run flow and every permission prompt with its reason text.

items.title: Brand assets
items.detail: Logo, app icon in all required sizes, launch/splash screen, favicon.

items.title: Copy and tone
items.detail: UI texts, error messages and the tone of voice; which languages.

items.title: Responsive layout
items.detail: Breakpoints and layout rules for phone, tablet and desktop widths.

items.title: Platform conventions
items.detail: Apple Human Interface Guidelines / Material Design: navigation, back, gestures, system controls.

items.title: Desktop conventions
items.detail: Menus, keyboard shortcuts, window sizes, tray/menu-bar behaviour per OS.

items.title: Command interface
items.detail: Commands, flags, help text, exit codes, human output and --json output.

items.title: Tech stack with sources
items.detail: Languages, frameworks and services with versions from a manifest or a cited source.

items.title: Layers and modules
items.detail: Three to five layers or a package map, one dependency direction, no cycles.

items.title: Data model
items.detail: Entities, fields, relations, indexes and ownership.

items.title: API design
items.detail: Endpoints or operations, payloads, errors, auth and versioning (REST, GraphQL or RPC).

items.title: Runtime map
items.detail: What runs on the device, on the server, in the cloud and at third parties.

items.title: Scale target
items.detail: Expected users and requests, and the limit the design holds before it must change.

items.title: Offline and sync
items.detail: Local store, sync trigger and the conflict rule.

items.title: Auth model
items.detail: Identity provider, sessions or tokens, roles and permissions.

items.title: Secrets plan
items.detail: Where every secret lives per environment; none in code, logs or app bundles.

items.title: Third-party services
items.detail: Payment, email, push, maps, AI and analytics providers with terms, region and costs.

items.title: Environments
items.detail: Development, staging and production with variable names (never values).

items.title: Decision records
items.detail: Every non-obvious choice as an ADR with alternatives.

items.title: Cross-platform approach
items.detail: React Native/Expo, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform or Tauri/Electron, and what stays native.

items.title: Realtime transport
items.detail: WebSockets or server-sent events, reconnect, ordering and presence.

items.title: Localisation strategy
items.detail: String catalogues, locale formats for dates and numbers, right-to-left.

items.title: AI integration
items.detail: Provider and model, where prompts live, cost limit per user, fallback; keys only on the server.

items.title: Task DAG
items.detail: board.json: tasks of complexity ≤ 6, one writer and scope each, no cycles, stages.

items.title: Policy
items.detail: policy.json: limits, protected paths (secrets, signing keys), manifests, approvals, denied commands.

items.title: Quality trace
items.detail: docs/quality.md: gates, D1..Dn and the trace D → task → acceptance → gate.

items.title: Build items mapped
items.detail: Every applicable build and verify item is linked to a task (factory.py link) or marked n/a.

items.title: Gate catalogue
items.detail: One docs/gates/<stack>.md per stack, commands verified from manifests or docs.

items.title: First briefs
items.detail: Briefs for the next three to five tasks; UI briefs with numbers.

items.title: Agent contract
items.detail: AGENTS.md with commands and rules; docs/orchestration.md with the task loop.

items.title: Repository
items.detail: Git repo, .gitignore (secrets, caches, .polier-slot), first commit on main.

items.title: Developer tooling
items.detail: IDE, package manager, formatter and linter named with their commands in AGENTS.md.

items.title: Branches and review
items.detail: task/<id> branches, review before merge, only the lead merges.

items.title: Cold start passed
items.detail: A fresh agent plans task one from the core files without a blocking question (prompt/rubric.md §4).

items.title: App shell and navigation
items.detail: Entry point, routing or navigation stack, layout frame.

items.title: State management
items.detail: How screens hold and share data; one pattern for the whole app.

items.title: Forms and validation
items.detail: Validation on the client for feedback and on the server for truth.

items.title: API client
items.detail: Typed calls with error handling, timeouts and retries with backoff.

items.title: Caching and offline mode
items.detail: Local cache, offline queue, sync on reconnect.

items.title: Localisation
items.detail: All UI strings from catalogues; dates, numbers and currency per locale.

items.title: Motion
items.detail: Animations and transitions with durations from the design rules; reduced-motion respected.

items.title: Server skeleton
items.detail: Framework setup, configuration from the environment, health endpoint.

items.title: Business logic
items.detail: Domain rules in the logic layer with unit tests.

items.title: Background jobs
items.detail: Queue for emails, imports and heavy work; retries and dead letters.

items.title: Scheduled tasks
items.detail: Cron-style jobs with locking so they never run twice.

items.title: Realtime channel
items.detail: Live updates with reconnect and authorisation per channel.

items.title: Rate limiting
items.detail: Per-user and per-IP limits, request size limits.

items.title: Schema and migrations
items.detail: Database schema created and changed only through versioned migrations.

items.title: File storage
items.detail: Uploads to object storage with size/type limits and signed URLs.

items.title: On-device store
items.detail: Local database (SQLite, SwiftData/Core Data, Room) with migrations.

items.title: Search
items.detail: Full-text or filtered search over the main entities.

items.title: Backup and restore
items.detail: Automated backups and a tested restore command.

items.title: Data export
items.detail: Users can download their data in a common format.

items.title: Sign up, log in, log out
items.detail: Account creation, session handling and logout on every device.

items.title: Password reset
items.detail: Reset or magic link with expiring single-use tokens.

items.title: Social login
items.detail: Sign in with Apple / Google; an iOS app with other social logins must offer Sign in with Apple or an equivalent [VERIFY: current App Review guideline 4.8].

items.title: Two-factor authentication
items.detail: TOTP or passkeys, recovery codes.

items.title: Roles and permissions
items.detail: Every access checked on the server, never only in the client.

items.title: Profile
items.detail: Users edit their profile and settings.

items.title: Account deletion
items.detail: Users delete their account and data from inside the product (store requirement for apps).

items.title: Encrypted transport
items.detail: HTTPS/TLS for every connection; HSTS on the web.

items.title: Password storage
items.detail: Passwords hashed with Argon2id or bcrypt, or delegated to the identity provider.

items.title: Secrets handling
items.detail: Secrets only from the environment or a secret manager; secret files in policy protected paths.

items.title: Input safety
items.detail: Validation and output encoding against SQL injection, XSS and CSRF.

items.title: Dependency audit
items.detail: npm audit, pip-audit or the stack's scanner as a CI gate.

items.title: Security headers
items.detail: CSP, CORS, frame and referrer policies.

items.title: Payments
items.detail: Stripe on the web, StoreKit on iOS, Play Billing on Android; receipts and webhooks verified on the server.

items.title: Transactional email
items.detail: Verification, reset and receipts through a provider with SPF/DKIM.

items.title: Push notifications
items.detail: APNs, FCM or Web Push with opt-in and per-topic settings.

items.title: AI calls
items.detail: Through the server, with per-user limits, timeouts and a fallback.

items.title: Analytics events
items.detail: A named event list, privacy-friendly tool, consent where required.

items.title: Maps and location
items.detail: Location only with permission and a reason text; coarse when fine is not needed.

items.title: SEO
items.detail: Titles, meta descriptions, sitemap, robots.txt, Open Graph, structured data.

items.title: Web performance
items.detail: Optimised images and fonts, Core Web Vitals budget in the gates.

items.title: Progressive web app
items.detail: Manifest and service worker for install and offline.

items.title: Consent banner
items.detail: Cookie/tracking consent before any non-essential tracking.

items.title: iOS permissions
items.detail: Usage-description strings in Info.plist for camera, photos, location, contacts, microphone.

items.title: iOS privacy manifest
items.detail: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy with tracking domains and required-reason APIs, also for SDKs.

items.title: Android permissions and target SDK
items.detail: Runtime permissions; targetSdk meets Google Play's current requirement [VERIFY: current Play target API level].

items.title: Android platform polish
items.detail: Adaptive icon, edge-to-edge layout, predictive back gesture.

items.title: Desktop auto-update
items.detail: Signed update feed and in-app updater.

items.title: Desktop packages
items.detail: Installer or package per OS (MSI/MSIX, DMG/pkg, AppImage/deb/rpm).

items.title: CLI basics
items.detail: --help, --version, documented exit codes, --json output, no prompts in pipes.

items.title: Service basics
items.detail: Health and readiness endpoints, graceful shutdown, configuration from the environment.

items.title: Unit tests
items.detail: Logic covered by unit tests that run as a gate in CI.

items.title: Integration tests
items.detail: API with a real test database per slot.

items.title: End-to-end tests
items.detail: D1..Dn as automated flows (Playwright, XCUITest, Espresso, Maestro).

items.title: Device matrix
items.detail: Smallest and largest supported screens, oldest supported OS, one real device per platform.

items.title: Browser matrix
items.detail: Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge and mobile Safari.

items.title: OS matrix
items.detail: Every supported Windows, macOS and Linux version.

items.title: Performance budget
items.detail: Start time, bundle size and response times measured against the budget.

items.title: Load test
items.detail: The scale target from the architecture, run alone as an exclusive gate.

items.title: Accessibility audit
items.detail: axe/Lighthouse on the web, VoiceOver and TalkBack on mobile.

items.title: Security review
items.detail: OWASP Top 10 (web/API) or MASVS (mobile) checklist, secret scan of the history.

items.title: Beta test
items.detail: Real users on TestFlight, a Play test track or a preview URL; findings triaged.

items.title: Independent review
items.detail: Every done task has reviews/<ID>.md with verdict: pass from a non-author.

items.title: Payment sandbox
items.detail: Purchase, refund, failed renewal and restore tested in the sandbox.

items.title: Offline and bad network
items.detail: Airplane mode, slow network and reconnect tested.

items.title: Localisation check
items.detail: Long strings, plural forms and locale formats in every language.

items.title: CI/CD
items.detail: Build, test and release in CI from tags only; agents never publish.

items.title: Versioning
items.detail: SemVer and a changelog entry per release.

items.title: Hosting
items.detail: Hosting for app, API and database chosen, with region and data residency.

items.title: Domain and TLS
items.detail: Domain, DNS records and an auto-renewing certificate.

items.title: Environments live
items.detail: Variables set per environment, smoke check passing (tools/smoke.py).

items.title: Privacy policy
items.detail: Per Swiss revFADP (and GDPR with EU users), linked in the product and the store listing.

items.title: Imprint
items.detail: Name, address and contact of the operator on the website.

items.title: Terms of service
items.detail: Terms of use; refunds and cancellation when money is taken.

items.title: Open-source licences
items.detail: Licences of all dependencies listed and compatible; notices shipped where required.

items.title: Processor agreements
items.detail: Data processing agreements with hosting, email, analytics and AI providers.

items.title: VAT and invoices
items.detail: VAT handling, invoices and refunds (stores handle this for in-app purchases).

items.title: Launch material
items.detail: Landing page, screenshots, short description, social posts.

items.title: Rollback
items.detail: Rollback steps written and tried once in staging.

items.title: Production web deploy
items.detail: CDN, caching headers, custom 404/500 pages, redirects.

items.title: Search registration
items.detail: Sitemap submitted to search consoles.

items.title: Apple Developer Program
items.detail: Membership active (yearly fee) for the publishing account.

items.title: iOS signing
items.detail: Bundle ID, certificates and provisioning profiles (automatic signing, Xcode Cloud or fastlane match).

items.title: App Store listing
items.detail: Name, subtitle, description, keywords, category, age rating, support URL and privacy policy URL (required for every app).

items.title: App Store screenshots
items.detail: Screenshots for the required device sizes; optional preview video.

items.title: App privacy details
items.detail: The App Store privacy label matches the privacy manifest and the real data flows.

items.title: TestFlight
items.detail: The release build tested through TestFlight.

items.title: App Review
items.detail: Review notes, demo account and a check against the App Review Guidelines.

items.title: In-app purchases
items.detail: Products and subscriptions configured in App Store Connect with StoreKit.

items.title: Export compliance
items.detail: Encryption questions answered (ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption).

items.title: Google Play Console
items.detail: Developer account with completed identity verification.

items.title: Android signing
items.detail: Application ID, upload key in a safe place, Play App Signing enabled.

items.title: Play Store listing
items.detail: Title, short and full description, icon, feature graphic, screenshots, category, contact, privacy policy URL.

items.title: Data safety form
items.detail: Play data safety section matches the real data flows.

items.title: Content rating
items.detail: Rating questionnaire and target audience completed.

items.title: Closed test
items.detail: Closed testing before production; new personal accounts need a minimum number of testers and days [VERIFY: current Play requirement].

items.title: Play Billing products
items.detail: In-app products and subscriptions configured in the Play Console.

items.title: Release bundle
items.detail: Signed AAB from CI with the required target API level.

items.title: Desktop code signing
items.detail: Windows Authenticode and macOS Developer ID certificates.

items.title: macOS notarisation
items.detail: Every macOS build notarised and stapled.

items.title: Distribution channel
items.detail: Website download, Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, winget or Homebrew.

items.title: Update feed
items.detail: Published update feed tested from the previous version.

items.title: Package published
items.detail: PyPI, npm, Homebrew or release binaries with checksums.

items.title: Error tracking
items.detail: Crashes and exceptions reported (Sentry, Crashlytics) without personal data.

items.title: Logging
items.detail: Structured logs with retention; no secrets or personal data in logs.

items.title: Uptime monitoring
items.detail: Health checks with alerts to a named person.

items.title: Backups watched
items.detail: Backup success monitored and a restore drill scheduled.

items.title: Support channel
items.detail: Email or form linked in the product and the store listing.

items.title: Feedback loop
items.detail: How feedback and bug reports become tasks on the board.

items.title: Usage review
items.detail: Analytics reviewed on a fixed cadence against the success signal.

items.title: Update cadence
items.detail: Dependency and security updates on a schedule (Dependabot or Renovate).

items.title: User help
items.detail: Help pages or FAQ for the main tasks.

items.title: Developer documentation
items.detail: README with setup, and docs/runbook.md for operations.

items.title: Cost alerts
items.detail: Budget alerts for hosting and paid APIs.

items.title: Incident plan
items.detail: Who does what when production is down; status communication.

items.title: Store upkeep
items.detail: Yearly OS/SDK updates and store policy changes tracked.

items.title: Data requests
items.detail: Access and deletion requests answered within the legal deadline.
